---

# Introduction

Episodic memory does not operate uniformly across continuous experience. Research in event
cognition proposes that the mind segments an ongoing flow of activity into discrete
**events** separated by **event boundaries** — moments when the prevailing situation model
must be updated (Zacks et al., 2007). According to Event Segmentation Theory (EST), these
boundaries arise when prediction errors in perceptual systems become large enough to
require a new event representation. Crucially, items encountered *at or near* event
boundaries are encoded more durably and later recognised with higher accuracy than items
experienced in the *middle* of an event (Swallow et al., 2009; Ben-Yakov & Dudai, 2011).

The boundary-memory advantage is well established for naturally structured events.
A less-studied question is whether it extends to boundaries that are *artificially
introduced* through film editing. Abrupt cuts between shots create strong perceptual
discontinuities that may force a situation-model update even when there is no genuine
narrative boundary — analogous to commercial breaks at non-boundaries impairing recall
(Boltz, 1992). Conversely, if the cut removes the natural endpoint of a scene, it may
*disrupt* encoding of immediately pre-boundary material.

The present study addresses this directly. Two groups watched short film clips differing
only in whether the clip ended with an **abrupt cut** (AB) 1–5 s before a consensus event
boundary, or with a **natural transition** (NB) at the original endpoint. A subsequent
recognition memory test probed two frame types: frames from just *before* a boundary
(**BB**, Before-Boundary) and frames from the *middle* of an event (**EM**, Event-Middle).

---

# Methods

## Participants

A total of **184 participants** were recruited from IIIT Hyderabad and randomly assigned
to one of two between-subjects conditions: Abrupt-cut (AB) or Natural-transition (NB). All
participants reported normal or corrected-to-normal vision.

The first 13 participants could not be included because of a data-collection error at the
start of the project — their files were never saved — leaving **171 usable data files**.
One file (sub42_NB) was excluded because the PsychoPy session returned no recognition
trial rows, leaving **170 files** (AB *n* = 81, NB *n* = 89) for screening.

Participants whose **encoding phase exceeded 27.05 minutes** were excluded as likely
inattentive viewers. This threshold was derived from the 5.6-minute contribution of five
repeated vigilance clips, plus an assumed 25-second skip latency per repetition. Four
participants exceeded the threshold. No participant scored at or below chance on the
recognition task. The final analysis sample was **N = 166 (AB *n* = 79, NB *n* = 87)**.

## Stimuli and Design

- **40 short video clips** were sourced from YouTube Shorts, each prepared in two
  versions: Abrupt-cut (AB) and Natural-transition (NB).  
  - **AB** clips were subtly cut 1–5 seconds *before* a consensus event boundary and
    resumed at the onset of a new event context.  
  - **NB** clips ended at their original, uninterrupted timelines. NB durations were
    adjusted so that mean duration matched the AB clips.
- Event boundaries and BB/EM probe locations were **already annotated in advance**
  (consensus annotation workflow) before this analysis pipeline was run.
- Five clips were repeated as **vigilance checks**; participants pressed the spacebar to
  skip these repeated videos (see `abruptmovies.csv` / `naturalmovies.csv`).
- For each clip, two still frames were extracted as recognition targets:
  - **BB** — frame from just *before* a consensus event boundary.
  - **EM** — frame from the *middle* of an event (positioned between two boundaries).
- Each target was paired with a visually similar, previously unseen **lure**, yielding
  **40 two-alternative forced-choice (2-AFC) trials** per participant. Lure similarity was
  manipulated across three levels (easy, moderate, difficult).

## Procedure

1. Participants passively watched their assigned clips during the encoding phase.
2. At test, each target was shown alongside its lure; participants indicated which image
   they had seen before.
3. Participants then gave a **confidence rating (1–5)**: 1 = not at all confident,
   5 = very confident.
4. Trial order was randomised. The experiment ran in PsychoPy.

## Research Questions and Predictions

| # | Research Question | Prediction |
|---|---|---|
| **RQ1** | Does viewing condition affect overall recognition accuracy and RT? | NB > AB accuracy; NB faster RT |
| **RQ2** | Does condition affect BB frame recognition? | BB accuracy NB > AB — abrupt cut falls close to BB, disrupting pre-boundary encoding |
| **RQ3** | Does condition affect EM frame recognition? | EM accuracy NB ~ AB — EM is far from the cut point, less sensitive to manipulation |

## Key Statistical Metrics

- **Recognition Memory Index (REC):** Bias-corrected discrimination index.  
  $\text{REC} = P(\text{"old"} \mid \text{Target}) - P(\text{"old"} \mid \text{Lure})$  
  REC = 0 → chance; REC = 1 → perfect discrimination.

- **Lure Discrimination Index (LDI):** Sensitivity to lure novelty.  
  $\text{LDI} = P(\text{"new"} \mid \text{Lure})$

## Analysis Approach

All analyses use R. This Phase 2 report includes **all available demographic variables**
(including handedness and vision) irrespective of their apparent relevance to memory.

Inferential testing combines non-parametric subject-level comparisons with a trial-level
binomial GLMM. Shapiro-Wilk tests on per-subject accuracy are retained as distribution
diagnostics for summary-level outcomes, while the condition × target-type effect is tested
using GLMM (logit link) with participant and item random intercepts (α = .05).

# Data Loading

## File paths

```{r paths}
data_root  <- "BRSM data csv"
sub_folder <- file.path(data_root, "BRSM data csv")

path_targets <- file.path(data_root, "target_and_lures.csv")
path_demog   <- file.path(data_root, "Demographic data.xlsx")
```

## Reference tables

```{r load-reference}
target_lures <- read_csv(path_targets, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(target_type = str_extract(target_img, "(?<=_)(EM|BB)(?=_T)"))

demog_raw <- read_excel(path_demog) %>%
  rename(sub_id_full = `Sub ID`) %>%
  mutate(sub_id_full = tolower(sub_id_full))

cat("Target/lure rows:", nrow(target_lures), "\n")
cat("Target types:\n")
print(table(target_lures$target_type))
```

## Subject CSVs

```{r load-subjects}
csv_files <- list.files(sub_folder, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
cat("CSV files found:", length(csv_files), "\n")

read_subject <- function(filepath) {
  fname     <- basename(filepath)
  sub_id    <- tolower(str_extract(fname, "^[Ss]ub\\d+"))
  condition <- str_extract(fname, "(?<=_)(AB|NB)(?=\\s?_)")

  df <- read_csv(filepath, show_col_types = FALSE,
                 col_types = cols(.default = "c"))

  if (!"movie_id" %in% names(df)) {
    warning(paste("Skipping", fname, "— no movie_id column"))
    return(NULL)
  }

  enc_start    <- suppressWarnings(
    as.numeric(df$instruction_2.stopped[!is.na(df$instruction_2.stopped)][1]))
  enc_end      <- suppressWarnings(
    as.numeric(df$Videos.stopped[!is.na(df$Videos.stopped)][1]))
  encoding_dur <- if (!is.na(enc_start) && !is.na(enc_end)) enc_end - enc_start else NA_real_

  df <- df %>% filter(!is.na(movie_id), movie_id != "")

  optional_cols <- list(
    is_repeat     = NA_integer_,  duration      = NA_real_,
    target_img    = NA_character_, lure_img     = NA_character_,
    confidence_rt = NA_real_
  )
  for (col in names(optional_cols))
    if (!col %in% names(df)) df[[col]] <- optional_cols[[col]]

  df %>%
    mutate(
      sub_id        = sub_id,
      condition     = condition,
      movie_id      = as.integer(movie_id),
      resp.corr     = as.numeric(resp.corr),
      resp.rt       = as.numeric(gsub("^\\[|\\]$", "", resp.rt)),
      confidence    = as.numeric(confidence),
      confidence_rt = as.numeric(confidence_rt),
      is_repeat     = as.integer(is_repeat),
      duration      = as.numeric(duration),
      encoding_dur  = encoding_dur
    ) %>%
    select(any_of(c("sub_id", "condition", "movie_id", "is_repeat", "duration",
                    "target_img", "lure_img",
                    "resp.keys", "resp.corr", "resp.rt",
                    "confidence", "confidence_rt", "encoding_dur")))
}

raw_data <- map_dfr(csv_files, read_subject)

cat("\nTotal trial rows loaded:", nrow(raw_data), "\n")
cat("Unique subjects loaded :", n_distinct(raw_data$sub_id), "\n\n")
cat("Condition breakdown:\n")
print(table(raw_data$condition))
```

## Join target type and demographics

```{r join-tables}
df <- raw_data %>%
  left_join(target_lures %>% select(movie_id, target_type), by = "movie_id")

demog <- demog_raw %>%
  mutate(sub_id = str_extract(sub_id_full, "^sub\\d+")) %>%
  select(sub_id, everything(), -sub_id_full)

demog_cols <- setdiff(names(demog), "sub_id")

df <- df %>% left_join(demog, by = "sub_id")
cat("Rows after join:", nrow(df), "\n")
```

# Data Cleaning and Quality Checks

## Trial count per subject

```{r trial-counts}
trial_counts <- df %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition) %>%
  summarise(n_trials = n(), .groups = "drop")

cat("Expected trials per subject: 40\n")
cat("Subjects with ≠ 40 trials:\n")
trial_counts %>% filter(n_trials != 40) %>% print()
cat("\nTrial count distribution:\n")
print(table(trial_counts$n_trials))
```

## Missing values in key columns

```{r missing-values}
key_cols <- c("resp.corr", "resp.rt", "confidence", "confidence_rt", "target_type")

df %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(key_cols), ~ sum(is.na(.)), .names = "NA_{.col}")) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Missing-value counts in key analysis columns") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

## Reaction time sanity check

```{r rt-check}
# Encoding-phase rows have no RT by design (resp.rt is NA); these are excluded from RT analyses.
rt_flags <- df %>% filter(is.na(resp.rt))
cat("Encoding-phase rows (no RT recorded):", nrow(rt_flags), "\n")

df %>%
  filter(!is.na(resp.rt)) %>%
  summarise(
    min_rt    = min(resp.rt),
    p5_rt     = quantile(resp.rt, 0.05),
    median_rt = median(resp.rt),
    p95_rt    = quantile(resp.rt, 0.95),
    max_rt    = max(resp.rt)
  ) %>%
  kbl(caption = "RT summary across all valid trials (seconds)", digits = 3) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

## Participant-level vigilance screening

```{r subject-accuracy}
VIGILANCE_THRESHOLD_S <- 27.05 * 60  # 1623 seconds

sub_accuracy <- df %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition) %>%
  summarise(
    n_trials     = n(),
    mean_acc     = mean(resp.corr, na.rm = TRUE),
    encoding_dur = first(encoding_dur),
    .groups      = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    REC            = 2 * mean_acc - 1,
    vigilance_fail = !is.na(encoding_dur) & encoding_dur > VIGILANCE_THRESHOLD_S
  )

vigilance_excluded <- sub_accuracy %>% filter(vigilance_fail)
cat("Subjects excluded for exceeding the vigilance threshold (> 27.05 min):",
    nrow(vigilance_excluded), "\n\n")

vigilance_excluded %>%
  select(sub_id, condition, encoding_dur) %>%
  mutate(encoding_min = round(encoding_dur / 60, 2)) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Vigilance-excluded participants",
      col.names = c("Subject", "Condition", "Encoding (s)", "Encoding (min)")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

```

Threshold = 27.05 min (5.6 min repeated videos + 25 s assumed skip latency × 5).

## Final cleaned data frame

```{r build-clean}
excluded_subs <- vigilance_excluded$sub_id

df_clean <- df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(resp.rt),
    !is.na(resp.corr),
    !(sub_id %in% excluded_subs)
  )

rt_mu <- mean(df_clean$resp.rt, na.rm = TRUE)
rt_sd <- sd(df_clean$resp.rt, na.rm = TRUE)
rt_low <- rt_mu - 3 * rt_sd
rt_high <- rt_mu + 3 * rt_sd

df_clean <- df_clean %>%
  mutate(rt_outlier_3sd = resp.rt < rt_low | resp.rt > rt_high)

df_rt_clean <- df_clean %>% filter(!rt_outlier_3sd)

cat(sprintf("RT 3-SD bounds: [%.3f, %.3f] seconds\n", rt_low, rt_high))
cat(sprintf("RT outlier trials removed (3-SD rule): %d of %d (%.2f%%)\n\n",
            sum(df_clean$rt_outlier_3sd, na.rm = TRUE),
            nrow(df_clean),
            100 * mean(df_clean$rt_outlier_3sd, na.rm = TRUE)))

cat("Total trials after cleaning :", nrow(df_clean), "\n")
cat("Total subjects after cleaning:", n_distinct(df_clean$sub_id), "\n\n")

df_rt_clean %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(Subjects = n_distinct(sub_id), Trials = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  kbl(caption = "Cleaned data for inferential analyses: subjects and trials by condition (3-SD outliers removed)",
      col.names = c("Condition", "Subjects", "Trials")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

# Descriptive Statistics

```{r sub-level-data}
# Subject-level summary — used in all plots and group-level tables below
sub_acc_conf <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_acc  = mean(resp.corr,  na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_conf = mean(confidence, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups   = "drop"
  )

sub_rt <- df_rt_clean %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition) %>%
  summarise(mean_rt = mean(resp.rt, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

sub_level <- sub_acc_conf %>%
  left_join(sub_rt, by = c("sub_id", "condition"))

# Retained participant demographics — derived from df_clean (post-exclusion only)
retained_subs <- df_clean %>%
  select(sub_id, condition, all_of(demog_cols)) %>%
  distinct()

# Sanity check: must equal final sample size
stopifnot(nrow(retained_subs) == 166)
cat(sprintf("Demographic rows: %d (matches final retained sample — demographics are post-exclusion only)\n",
            nrow(retained_subs)))

# Consistent colour palette
cols <- c(AB = "#E07B54", NB = "#5B8DB8")
```

## Demographics

```{r demog-summary}
# Overall missingness profile for every demographic field
retained_subs %>%
  select(all_of(demog_cols)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value",
    values_transform = list(Value = as.character)
  ) %>%
  mutate(Value = as.character(Value),
         is_missing = is.na(Value) | trimws(Value) == "") %>%
  group_by(Variable) %>%
  summarise(
    Non_missing = sum(!is_missing),
    Missing     = sum(is_missing),
    Missing_pct = round(100 * mean(is_missing), 2),
    .groups     = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Missing_pct), Variable) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Demographic completeness (all available fields)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

# Age summary by condition (if available)
if ("Age" %in% names(retained_subs)) {
  retained_subs %>%
    group_by(condition) %>%
    summarise(
      n        = n(),
      Mean_Age = round(mean(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
      SD       = round(sd(Age,  na.rm = TRUE), 1),
      Min      = min(Age, na.rm = TRUE),
      Max      = max(Age, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups  = "drop"
    ) %>%
    kbl(caption = "Age summary by condition") %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
}

# Full categorical breakdown for all non-age demographic fields
cat_vars <- setdiff(demog_cols, "Age")

retained_subs %>%
  select(condition, all_of(cat_vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(cat_vars),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value",
    values_transform = list(Value = as.character)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Value = as.character(Value),
    Value = ifelse(is.na(Value) | trimws(Value) == "", "(not reported)", Value)
  ) %>%
  count(Variable, condition, Value, name = "n") %>%

      col.names = c("Variable", "Condition", "Category", "Count", "Percent")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

# Pooled full-sample demographic distribution
retained_subs %>%
  select(all_of(cat_vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value",
    values_transform = list(Value = as.character)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Value = as.character(Value),
    Value = ifelse(is.na(Value) | trimws(Value) == "", "(not reported)", Value)
  ) %>%

  group_by(Variable) %>%
  mutate(Percent = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(Variable, desc(n)) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Pooled demographic distribution (all non-age fields)",
      col.names = c("Variable", "Category", "Count", "Percent")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

if (all(c("Handedness", "Vision") %in% names(retained_subs))) {
  hv_na <- retained_subs %>%
    summarise(
      Handedness_missing = sum(is.na(Handedness) | trimws(as.character(Handedness)) == ""),

    )
  cat(sprintf("Missing Handedness entries: %d\n", hv_na$Handedness_missing))
  cat(sprintf("Missing Vision entries: %d\n", hv_na$Vision_missing))
}

# Backward-compatible count for Gender missingness (if available)
if ("Gender" %in% names(retained_subs)) {
  n_gender_na <- sum(is.na(retained_subs$Gender) | trimws(as.character(retained_subs$Gender)) == "")
  cat(sprintf("Participants with missing gender: %d\n", n_gender_na))
}
```

## Demographic Balance Checks

Before testing the main memory hypotheses, we verify that AB and NB groups are
comparable across available demographics. These checks are quality-control diagnostics,
not the primary hypothesis tests.

### Age balance: Mann–Whitney *U* test

Age is a continuous variable that could potentially influence memory performance.
A Mann–Whitney *U* test is used (rather than an independent-samples *t*-test) because it
does not assume normality and is consistent with the non-parametric approach adopted
throughout this study. A non-significant result (p > .05) confirms that age is balanced
across conditions.

```{r demog-age-balance}
if ("Age" %in% names(retained_subs)) {
  age_AB <- retained_subs %>% filter(condition == "AB") %>% pull(Age)
  age_NB <- retained_subs %>% filter(condition == "NB") %>% pull(Age)

  wt_age <- wilcox.test(age_AB, age_NB, exact = FALSE)

  cat("Mann-Whitney U test — Age (AB vs NB)\n")
  cat(sprintf("W = %.1f,  p = %.4f\n\n", wt_age$statistic, wt_age$p.value))

  if (wt_age$p.value > .05) {
    cat("Interpretation: Groups do NOT differ significantly in age (p > .05).\n")
  } else {
    cat("WARNING: Groups differ significantly in age (p <= .05).\n")
  }
}
```

### Categorical demographics: Chi-square/Fisher balance checks

For each non-age demographic variable, AB and NB distributions are compared. Fisher's
exact test is used when sparse cells are present.

```{r demog-gender-balance}
cat_balance <- map_dfr(setdiff(demog_cols, "Age"), function(var_name) {
  tmp <- retained_subs %>%
    mutate(value = .data[[var_name]],
           value = as.character(value),
           value = ifelse(is.na(value) | trimws(value) == "", "(not reported)", value))

  tab <- table(tmp$condition, tmp$value)

  if (all(dim(tab) > 1)) {
    if (any(tab < 5)) {
      tst <- fisher.test(tab)
      tibble(
        Variable = var_name,
        Test = "Fisher exact",
        Statistic = NA_real_,
        p_value = as.numeric(tst$p.value)
      )
    } else {
      tst <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab))
      tibble(
        Variable = var_name,
        Test = "Chi-square",
        Statistic = as.numeric(tst$statistic),
        p_value = as.numeric(tst$p.value)
      )
    }
  } else {
    tibble(
      Variable = var_name,
      Test = "Not testable (single category)",
      Statistic = NA_real_,
      p_value = NA_real_
    )
  }
})

cat_balance %>%
  mutate(
    Statistic = round(Statistic, 3),
    p_value = round(p_value, 4),
    Balanced = ifelse(is.na(p_value), "NA", ifelse(p_value > .05, "Yes", "No"))
  ) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Categorical demographic balance checks by condition") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

### Balance check summary

```{r demog-balance-summary}
age_summary_tbl <- if ("Age" %in% names(retained_subs)) {
  tibble(
    Variable = "Age",
    Test = "Mann-Whitney U",
    Statistic = round(as.numeric(wt_age$statistic), 1),
    p_value = round(as.numeric(wt_age$p.value), 4),
    Balanced = ifelse(wt_age$p.value > .05, "Yes", "No")
  )
} else {
  tibble(
    Variable = "Age",
    Test = "Unavailable",
    Statistic = NA_real_,
    p_value = NA_real_,
    Balanced = "NA"
  )
}

balance_summary <- bind_rows(
  age_summary_tbl,
  cat_balance %>%
    transmute(
      Variable,
      Test,
      Statistic = round(Statistic, 3),
      p_value = round(p_value, 4),
      Balanced = ifelse(is.na(p_value), "NA", ifelse(p_value > .05, "Yes", "No"))
    )
)

balance_summary %>%
  kbl(caption = "Demographic balance between AB and NB conditions",
      col.names = c("Variable", "Test", "Statistic", "p-value", "Balanced?")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

## Recognition accuracy by condition

```{r acc-by-condition}
acc_condition <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition) %>%
  summarise(mean_acc = mean(resp.corr, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(
    n      = n(),
    Mean   = round(mean(mean_acc), 3),
    SD     = round(sd(mean_acc),   3),
    SE     = round(sd(mean_acc) / sqrt(n()), 3),
    Median = round(median(mean_acc), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

acc_condition %>%
  kbl(caption = "Recognition accuracy by condition",
      col.names = c("Condition", "N", "Mean", "SD", "SE", "Median")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

AB = **83.8%**, NB = **87.0%** — a 3.2 percentage-point advantage for the
natural-transition condition.

## Recognition accuracy by condition × target type

```{r acc-by-target-type}
acc_target <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition, target_type) %>%
  summarise(mean_acc = mean(resp.corr, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(condition, target_type) %>%
  summarise(
    n    = n(),
    Mean = round(mean(mean_acc), 3),
    SD   = round(sd(mean_acc),   3),
    SE   = round(sd(mean_acc) / sqrt(n()), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

acc_target %>%
  kbl(caption = "Recognition accuracy by condition and target type",
      col.names = c("Condition", "Target type", "N", "Mean", "SD", "SE")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

- NB > AB for **BB** frames: 85.8% vs 82.2% (gap = 3.6 pp) — consistent with RQ2.
- NB > AB for **EM** frames: 88.3% vs 85.4% (gap = 2.9 pp) — descriptively smaller than BB; inferential testing below determines whether this difference is reliable.
- EM > BB within both conditions (EM targets are farther from the cut, easier to encode).

## Recognition Memory Index (REC) by condition

```{r rec-index}
# REC = P("old"|Target) - P("old"|Lure)
# Since the 2-AFC response is coded as correct/incorrect for the target,
# P("old"|Lure) = 1 - mean_acc
rec_summary <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition) %>%
  summarise(
    p_old_target = mean(resp.corr, na.rm = TRUE),
    p_old_lure   = 1 - mean(resp.corr, na.rm = TRUE),
    REC          = p_old_target - p_old_lure,
    .groups      = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(
    n        = n(),
    Mean_REC = round(mean(REC), 3),
    SD_REC   = round(sd(REC),   3),
    SE_REC   = round(sd(REC) / sqrt(n()), 3),
    .groups  = "drop"
  )

rec_summary %>%
  kbl(caption = "Recognition Memory Index (REC = 2*Acc - 1) by condition",
      col.names = c("Condition", "N", "Mean REC", "SD", "SE")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

## Lure Discrimination Index (LDI) by condition

The **general LDI formula** from the Mnemonic Similarity Task (MST) literature
(Bakker et al., 2008) is:

$$\text{LDI} = P(\text{"similar"} \mid \text{Lure}) - P(\text{"similar"} \mid \text{Foil})$$

This requires **three item types** (targets, lures, foils) and a **three-option
response** ("old" / "similar" / "new") so the foil term can correct for response
bias.

**Why we use a different formula here:** This experiment used a **2-AFC design**
— each trial presented one target and one lure side-by-side and the participant
made a binary forced choice. There are no foil items and no "similar" response
category, so the MST formula cannot be applied. Instead:

$$\text{LDI} = P(\text{"new"} \mid \text{Lure}) = P(\text{correct})$$

In a 2-AFC, choosing the target *is* rejecting the lure, so LDI is numerically
identical to mean accuracy. It is computed and reported here for terminological
consistency with the pattern separation literature, but **provides no additional
information beyond the accuracy analysis**.

```{r ldi-index}
# LDI = P("new" | Lure) = probability of correctly rejecting a lure
# In 2-AFC: a "correct" response (resp.corr = 1) means the participant
# chose the target, i.e., they correctly called the lure "new".
# So LDI per trial = resp.corr  (same column, different interpretation).
# Subject-level LDI = mean(resp.corr) across all trials = mean accuracy.
# We compute it explicitly here for clarity and report it separately.
# NOTE: The standard MST formula (P("similar"|Lure) - P("similar"|Foil))
# cannot be applied here due to the 2-AFC design (no foils, no "similar" option).

ldi_summary <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition) %>%
  summarise(
    LDI = mean(resp.corr, na.rm = TRUE),   # P("new" | Lure) = P(correct)
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(
    n        = n(),
    Mean_LDI = round(mean(LDI), 3),
    SD_LDI   = round(sd(LDI),   3),
    SE_LDI   = round(sd(LDI) / sqrt(n()), 3),
    Min_LDI  = round(min(LDI), 3),
    Max_LDI  = round(max(LDI), 3),
    .groups  = "drop"
  )

ldi_summary %>%
  kbl(caption = "Lure Discrimination Index (LDI = P('new' | Lure)) by condition",
      col.names = c("Condition", "N", "Mean LDI", "SD", "SE", "Min", "Max")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

cat("\nInterpretation:\n")
cat(sprintf("AB: Mean LDI = %.3f (SD = %.3f)\n",
            ldi_summary$Mean_LDI[ldi_summary$condition == "AB"],
            ldi_summary$SD_LDI[ldi_summary$condition == "AB"]))
cat(sprintf("NB: Mean LDI = %.3f (SD = %.3f)\n",
            ldi_summary$Mean_LDI[ldi_summary$condition == "NB"],
            ldi_summary$SD_LDI[ldi_summary$condition == "NB"]))
cat("LDI > 0.5 indicates above-chance lure rejection in both conditions.\n")
```

# Normality Testing

Before selecting inferential tests we assess whether per-subject recognition accuracy
is normally distributed within each condition. Because accuracy is bounded in [0, 1]
and is commonly ceiling-skewed in memory paradigms, normality cannot be assumed a priori.

## Shapiro-Wilk test

```{r normality-shapiro}
acc_AB <- sub_level %>% filter(condition == "AB") %>% pull(mean_acc)
acc_NB <- sub_level %>% filter(condition == "NB") %>% pull(mean_acc)

sw_AB <- shapiro.test(acc_AB)
sw_NB <- shapiro.test(acc_NB)

cat("Shapiro-Wilk Normality Test\n")
cat(sprintf("AB: W = %.4f,  p = %.4f\n", sw_AB$statistic, sw_AB$p.value))
cat(sprintf("NB: W = %.4f,  p = %.4f\n\n", sw_NB$statistic, sw_NB$p.value))

tribble(
  ~Group, ~W,                      ~p,                       ~Normal,
  "AB",   round(sw_AB$statistic, 3), round(sw_AB$p.value, 4), "No",
  "NB",   round(sw_NB$statistic, 3), round(sw_NB$p.value, 4), "No"
) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Shapiro-Wilk normality test results",
      col.names = c("Group", "W", "p-value", "Normal?")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  column_spec(4, bold = TRUE, color = "red")

cat("\nConclusion:\n")
cat("Both conditions violate normality (p < .05).\n")
cat("For between-group comparisons of subject-level accuracy, non-parametric tests are preferred.\n")
cat("Trial-level effects are modeled with a binomial GLMM, which does not require normality of accuracy scores.\n")
```

## QQ plots

```{r qq-plots, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

qqnorm(acc_AB, main = "Q-Q Plot — AB condition",
       pch = 16, col = "#E07B54", cex = 0.9)
qqline(acc_AB, col = "red", lwd = 2)
mtext(sprintf("W = %.3f,  p = %.4f", sw_AB$statistic, sw_AB$p.value),
      side = 3, line = -1.5, cex = 0.85, col = "grey30")

qqnorm(acc_NB, main = "Q-Q Plot — NB condition",
       pch = 16, col = "#5B8DB8", cex = 0.9)
qqline(acc_NB, col = "red", lwd = 2)
mtext(sprintf("W = %.3f,  p = %.4f", sw_NB$statistic, sw_NB$p.value),
      side = 3, line = -1.5, cex = 0.85, col = "grey30")

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

Points depart from the diagonal reference line in the upper tail of both distributions,
confirming ceiling-skew. This departure is consistent with the Shapiro-Wilk rejection of
normality.

# Phase 2 Inferential Analyses

All inferential tests below are run on the RT 3-SD filtered dataset
(`df_rt_clean`) for consistency across hypotheses.

## RQ1: Overall AB vs NB (accuracy and RT)

```{r inferential-rq1}
subject_acc <- df_rt_clean %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition) %>%
  summarise(mean_acc = mean(resp.corr, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

subject_rt <- df_rt_clean %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition) %>%
  summarise(mean_rt = mean(resp.rt, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

mw_acc <- wilcox.test(mean_acc ~ condition, data = subject_acc, exact = FALSE)
mw_rt <- wilcox.test(mean_rt ~ condition, data = subject_rt, exact = FALSE)

rbc_unpaired <- function(w, n1, n2) {
  2 * as.numeric(w) / (n1 * n2) - 1
}

n_ab_acc <- subject_acc %>% filter(condition == "AB") %>% nrow()
n_nb_acc <- subject_acc %>% filter(condition == "NB") %>% nrow()
n_ab_rt <- subject_rt %>% filter(condition == "AB") %>% nrow()
n_nb_rt <- subject_rt %>% filter(condition == "NB") %>% nrow()

rq1_tbl <- tibble(
  Outcome = c("Overall accuracy", "Overall RT"),
  Test = c("Mann-Whitney U", "Mann-Whitney U"),
  Statistic_W = c(as.numeric(mw_acc$statistic), as.numeric(mw_rt$statistic)),
  p_value = c(as.numeric(mw_acc$p.value), as.numeric(mw_rt$p.value)),
  Rank_biserial_r = c(
    rbc_unpaired(mw_acc$statistic, n_ab_acc, n_nb_acc),
    rbc_unpaired(mw_rt$statistic, n_ab_rt, n_nb_rt)
  )
) %>%
  mutate(across(c(Statistic_W, p_value, Rank_biserial_r), ~ round(., 4)))

rq1_tbl %>%
  kbl(caption = "RQ1 inferential tests: AB vs NB (overall outcomes)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r inferential-rq1-viz, fig.width=12, fig.height=5}
    x = "Condition", y = "Subject mean accuracy"
  ) +

  geom_boxplot(width = 0.20, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.85) +

  labs(
    title = sprintf("Overall RT by condition (Mann-Whitney p = %.4f)", mw_rt$p.value),
    x = "Condition", y = "Subject mean RT (s)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

(p_rq1_acc | p_rq1_rt)
```

**Observation (RQ1):**
Overall recognition accuracy differs significantly by condition (*p* = `r sprintf("%.4f", mw_acc$p.value)`), with
NB showing better performance than AB. Overall RT does not differ significantly
(*p* = `r sprintf("%.4f", mw_rt$p.value)`), indicating that the condition effect is primarily on accuracy, not speed.

## RQ2 and RQ3: Between-condition tests for BB and EM

```{r inferential-rq23}
sub_by_type <- df_rt_clean %>%
  filter(target_type %in% c("BB", "EM")) %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition, target_type) %>%
  summarise(mean_acc = mean(resp.corr, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

bb_data <- sub_by_type %>% filter(target_type == "BB")
em_data <- sub_by_type %>% filter(target_type == "EM")

mw_bb <- wilcox.test(mean_acc ~ condition, data = bb_data, exact = FALSE)
mw_em <- wilcox.test(mean_acc ~ condition, data = em_data, exact = FALSE)

n_ab_bb <- bb_data %>% filter(condition == "AB") %>% nrow()
n_nb_bb <- bb_data %>% filter(condition == "NB") %>% nrow()
n_ab_em <- em_data %>% filter(condition == "AB") %>% nrow()
n_nb_em <- em_data %>% filter(condition == "NB") %>% nrow()

rq23_tbl <- tibble(
  Contrast = c("BB accuracy: NB vs AB", "EM accuracy: NB vs AB"),
  Test = c("Mann-Whitney U", "Mann-Whitney U"),
  Statistic_W = c(as.numeric(mw_bb$statistic), as.numeric(mw_em$statistic)),
  p_value = c(as.numeric(mw_bb$p.value), as.numeric(mw_em$p.value)),
  Rank_biserial_r = c(
    rbc_unpaired(mw_bb$statistic, n_ab_bb, n_nb_bb),
    rbc_unpaired(mw_em$statistic, n_ab_em, n_nb_em)
  )
) %>%
  mutate(across(c(Statistic_W, p_value, Rank_biserial_r), ~ round(., 4)))

rq23_tbl %>%
  kbl(caption = "RQ2/RQ3 inferential tests: target-type specific between-condition contrasts") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

### RQ2/RQ3 visualisation

```{r inferential-rq23-viz, fig.width=12, fig.height=5}
p_rq23_dist <- ggplot(sub_by_type,
                      aes(x = condition, y = mean_acc, fill = condition)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.25, trim = TRUE) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.20, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.10, size = 1.2, alpha = 0.35) +
  facet_wrap(~ target_type, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Condition differences within BB and EM",
    subtitle = sprintf("BB p = %.4f | EM p = %.4f", mw_bb$p.value, mw_em$p.value),
    x = "Condition", y = "Subject mean accuracy"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

p_rq23_effect <- rq23_tbl %>%
  transmute(
    Contrast,
    Rank_biserial_r = as.numeric(Rank_biserial_r)
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Contrast, y = Rank_biserial_r, fill = Contrast)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.55, alpha = 0.85, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.8) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-1, 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Effect direction and size (rank-biserial r)",
    x = NULL, y = "Rank-biserial r"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

(p_rq23_dist | p_rq23_effect)
```

**Observation (RQ2/RQ3 between-condition):**
NB outperforms AB for both BB (*p* = `r sprintf("%.4f", mw_bb$p.value)`) and EM (*p* = `r sprintf("%.4f", mw_em$p.value)`) target types.
The effect sizes are modest in magnitude but consistently in the NB-favouring direction.

## TA check: EM > BB within each condition

```{r inferential-em-greater-bb}
ab_pairs <- sub_by_type %>%
  filter(condition == "AB") %>%
  select(sub_id, target_type, mean_acc) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = target_type, values_from = mean_acc) %>%
  drop_na(BB, EM)

nb_pairs <- sub_by_type %>%
  filter(condition == "NB") %>%
  select(sub_id, target_type, mean_acc) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = target_type, values_from = mean_acc) %>%
  drop_na(BB, EM)

wil_ab <- wilcox.test(ab_pairs$EM, ab_pairs$BB,
                      paired = TRUE, alternative = "greater", exact = FALSE)
wil_nb <- wilcox.test(nb_pairs$EM, nb_pairs$BB,
                      paired = TRUE, alternative = "greater", exact = FALSE)

tibble(
  Condition = c("AB", "NB"),
  Comparison = c("EM > BB", "EM > BB"),
  Test = c("Paired Wilcoxon (one-sided)", "Paired Wilcoxon (one-sided)"),
  Statistic_V = c(as.numeric(wil_ab$statistic), as.numeric(wil_nb$statistic)),
  p_value = c(as.numeric(wil_ab$p.value), as.numeric(wil_nb$p.value))
) %>%
  mutate(across(c(Statistic_V, p_value), ~ round(., 4))) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Within-condition tests for TA request: EM greater than BB") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

## Condition × target-type interaction (GLMM replacement for mixed ANOVA)

```{r inferential-glmm}
glmm_data <- df_rt_clean %>%
  filter(target_type %in% c("BB", "EM"), condition %in% c("AB", "NB")) %>%
  mutate(
    condition = factor(condition, levels = c("AB", "NB")),
    target_type = factor(target_type, levels = c("EM", "BB")),
    sub_id = factor(sub_id),
    movie_id = factor(movie_id),
    resp.corr = as.integer(resp.corr)
  )

glmm_fit <- glmer(
  resp.corr ~ condition * target_type + (1 | sub_id) + (1 | movie_id),
  data = glmm_data,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))
)

coef_tbl <- as.data.frame(summary(glmm_fit)$coefficients) %>%
  rownames_to_column("Term") %>%
  transmute(
    Term,
    Estimate_logit = Estimate,
    SE = `Std. Error`,
    z = `z value`,
    p_value = `Pr(>|z|)`,
    OR = exp(Estimate),
    OR_CI_low = exp(Estimate - 1.96 * `Std. Error`),
    OR_CI_high = exp(Estimate + 1.96 * `Std. Error`)
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 4)))

coef_tbl %>%
  kbl(caption = "Binomial GLMM coefficients (odds ratios and 95% Wald CI)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

glmm_no_int <- update(glmm_fit, . ~ . - condition:target_type)
glmm_lrt <- anova(glmm_no_int, glmm_fit, test = "Chisq")

interaction_tbl <- tibble(
  Comparison = "Interaction term added: condition × target_type",
  Chi_sq = as.numeric(glmm_lrt$Chisq[2]),
  df = as.numeric(glmm_lrt$Df[2]),
  p_value = as.numeric(glmm_lrt$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2])
) %>%
  mutate(across(c(Chi_sq, df, p_value), ~ round(., 4)))

interaction_tbl %>%
  kbl(caption = "GLMM likelihood-ratio test for interaction") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

### GLMM visualisation

```{r inferential-glmm-viz, fig.width=12, fig.height=5}
coef_plot_df <- coef_tbl %>%
  filter(Term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(Term = recode(
    Term,
    "conditionNB" = "Condition: NB vs AB",
    "target_typeBB" = "Target type: BB vs EM",
    "conditionNB:target_typeBB" = "Interaction: NB × BB"
  ))

p_glmm_or <- ggplot(coef_plot_df,
                    aes(y = fct_rev(factor(Term)), x = OR)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey35") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = OR_CI_low, xmax = OR_CI_high), height = 0.18, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 2.8, colour = "#2C7FB8") +
  labs(
    title = "GLMM coefficient forest plot (odds ratios)",
    x = "Odds ratio (95% Wald CI)", y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

newdat <- expand_grid(
  condition = factor(c("AB", "NB"), levels = c("AB", "NB")),
  target_type = factor(c("EM", "BB"), levels = c("EM", "BB"))
)

X <- model.matrix(~ condition * target_type, data = newdat)
beta <- fixef(glmm_fit)
V <- as.matrix(vcov(glmm_fit))

eta <- as.vector(X %*% beta)
se_eta <- sqrt(diag(X %*% V %*% t(X)))

pred_df <- newdat %>%
  mutate(
    pred_prob = plogis(eta),
    ci_low = plogis(eta - 1.96 * se_eta),
    ci_high = plogis(eta + 1.96 * se_eta)
  )

p_glmm_pred <- ggplot(pred_df,
                      aes(x = target_type, y = pred_prob,
                          group = condition, colour = condition)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_low, ymax = ci_high), width = 0.10, linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    title = sprintf("Model-predicted accuracy by condition × target type (interaction p = %.4f)",
                    interaction_tbl$p_value[1]),
    x = "Target type", y = "Predicted probability of correct response",
    colour = "Condition"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

(p_glmm_or | p_glmm_pred)
```

**Observation (GLMM):**
The GLMM shows a significant main effect of condition (NB > AB; OR = `r sprintf("%.2f", coef_tbl$OR[coef_tbl$Term == "conditionNB"])`,
*p* = `r sprintf("%.4f", coef_tbl$p_value[coef_tbl$Term == "conditionNB"])`), no significant main effect of target type, and no significant
condition × target-type interaction (LRT *p* = `r sprintf("%.4f", interaction_tbl$p_value[1])`). Thus, NB confers a general
accuracy benefit, but this benefit is not selectively larger for BB than EM.

## Confidence-accuracy association (Spearman)

```{r inferential-spearman}
sub_conf <- df_rt_clean %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_acc = mean(resp.corr, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_conf = mean(confidence, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

sp_all <- cor.test(sub_conf$mean_conf, sub_conf$mean_acc,
                   method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)

sp_by_cond <- sub_conf %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(
    rho = cor(mean_conf, mean_acc, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
    p_value = cor.test(mean_conf, mean_acc, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)$p.value,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

bind_rows(
  tibble(
    Scope = "All participants",
    rho = as.numeric(sp_all$estimate),
    p_value = as.numeric(sp_all$p.value)
  ),
  sp_by_cond %>% rename(Scope = condition)
) %>%
  mutate(across(c(rho, p_value), ~ round(., 4))) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Spearman confidence-accuracy association") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

### Spearman visualisation

```{r inferential-spearman-viz, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
ggplot(sub_conf,
       aes(x = mean_conf, y = mean_acc, colour = condition)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.70, size = 2.1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1.0) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(1, 5), breaks = 1:5) +
  labs(
    title = sprintf("Confidence vs accuracy (Spearman rho all = %.3f, p = %.4f)",
                    as.numeric(sp_all$estimate), as.numeric(sp_all$p.value)),
    x = "Subject mean confidence", y = "Subject mean accuracy",
    colour = "Condition"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

  **Observation (confidence-accuracy):**
  Confidence positively tracks accuracy overall (Spearman $\rho$ = `r sprintf("%.4f", as.numeric(sp_all$estimate))`,
  `r if (sp_all$p.value < 0.001) "*p* < 0.001" else paste0("*p* = ", sprintf("%.4f", sp_all$p.value))`), and this relationship is significant in both AB and NB groups.
  Participants therefore show meaningful metacognitive sensitivity in both conditions.

## Sensitivity analysis: with vs without RT outlier filtering

```{r sensitivity-table}
# Recompute key inferential tests on unfiltered data (df_clean) for comparison.
subject_acc_raw <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition) %>%
  summarise(mean_acc = mean(resp.corr, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

subject_rt_raw <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition) %>%
  summarise(mean_rt = mean(resp.rt, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

mw_acc_raw <- wilcox.test(mean_acc ~ condition, data = subject_acc_raw, exact = FALSE)
mw_rt_raw <- wilcox.test(mean_rt ~ condition, data = subject_rt_raw, exact = FALSE)

sub_by_type_raw <- df_clean %>%
  filter(target_type %in% c("BB", "EM")) %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition, target_type) %>%
  summarise(mean_acc = mean(resp.corr, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

bb_data_raw <- sub_by_type_raw %>% filter(target_type == "BB")
em_data_raw <- sub_by_type_raw %>% filter(target_type == "EM")

mw_bb_raw <- wilcox.test(mean_acc ~ condition, data = bb_data_raw, exact = FALSE)
mw_em_raw <- wilcox.test(mean_acc ~ condition, data = em_data_raw, exact = FALSE)

ab_pairs_raw <- sub_by_type_raw %>%
  filter(condition == "AB") %>%
  select(sub_id, target_type, mean_acc) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = target_type, values_from = mean_acc) %>%
  drop_na(BB, EM)

nb_pairs_raw <- sub_by_type_raw %>%
  filter(condition == "NB") %>%
  select(sub_id, target_type, mean_acc) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = target_type, values_from = mean_acc) %>%
  drop_na(BB, EM)

wil_ab_raw <- wilcox.test(ab_pairs_raw$EM, ab_pairs_raw$BB,
                          paired = TRUE, alternative = "greater", exact = FALSE)
wil_nb_raw <- wilcox.test(nb_pairs_raw$EM, nb_pairs_raw$BB,
                          paired = TRUE, alternative = "greater", exact = FALSE)

glmm_data_raw <- df_clean %>%
  filter(target_type %in% c("BB", "EM"), condition %in% c("AB", "NB")) %>%
  mutate(
    condition = factor(condition, levels = c("AB", "NB")),
    target_type = factor(target_type, levels = c("EM", "BB")),
    sub_id = factor(sub_id),
    movie_id = factor(movie_id),
    resp.corr = as.integer(resp.corr)
  )

glmm_fit_raw <- glmer(
  resp.corr ~ condition * target_type + (1 | sub_id) + (1 | movie_id),
  data = glmm_data_raw,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))
)

coef_tbl_raw <- as.data.frame(summary(glmm_fit_raw)$coefficients) %>%
  rownames_to_column("Term")

p_condition_raw <- coef_tbl_raw %>%
  filter(Term == "conditionNB") %>%
  pull(`Pr(>|z|)`) %>%
  as.numeric()

glmm_no_int_raw <- update(glmm_fit_raw, . ~ . - condition:target_type)
glmm_lrt_raw <- anova(glmm_no_int_raw, glmm_fit_raw, test = "Chisq")
p_interaction_raw <- as.numeric(glmm_lrt_raw$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2])

sub_conf_raw <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_acc = mean(resp.corr, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_conf = mean(confidence, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

sp_all_raw <- cor.test(sub_conf_raw$mean_conf, sub_conf_raw$mean_acc,
                       method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)

fmt_p <- function(p) {
  ifelse(p < 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("%.4f", p))
}

sensitivity_tbl <- tibble(
  Analysis = c(
    "RQ1 overall accuracy (Mann-Whitney U)",
    "RQ1 overall RT (Mann-Whitney U)",
    "RQ2 BB accuracy (Mann-Whitney U)",
    "RQ3 EM accuracy (Mann-Whitney U)",
    "EM > BB within AB (paired Wilcoxon)",
    "EM > BB within NB (paired Wilcoxon)",
    "GLMM condition main effect (conditionNB)",
    "GLMM interaction (LRT condition × target_type)",
    "Spearman confidence-accuracy (overall)"
  ),
  p_unfiltered = c(
    as.numeric(mw_acc_raw$p.value),
    as.numeric(mw_rt_raw$p.value),
    as.numeric(mw_bb_raw$p.value),
    as.numeric(mw_em_raw$p.value),
    as.numeric(wil_ab_raw$p.value),
    as.numeric(wil_nb_raw$p.value),
    p_condition_raw,
    p_interaction_raw,
    as.numeric(sp_all_raw$p.value)
  ),
  p_filtered = c(
    as.numeric(mw_acc$p.value),
    as.numeric(mw_rt$p.value),
    as.numeric(mw_bb$p.value),
    as.numeric(mw_em$p.value),
    as.numeric(wil_ab$p.value),
    as.numeric(wil_nb$p.value),
    as.numeric(coef_tbl$p_value[coef_tbl$Term == "conditionNB"]),
    as.numeric(interaction_tbl$p_value[1]),
    as.numeric(sp_all$p.value)
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    Sig_unfiltered = ifelse(p_unfiltered < 0.05, "Yes", "No"),
    Sig_filtered = ifelse(p_filtered < 0.05, "Yes", "No"),
    Decision_stable = ifelse(Sig_unfiltered == Sig_filtered, "Yes", "No"),
    p_unfiltered = fmt_p(p_unfiltered),
    p_filtered = fmt_p(p_filtered)
  )

sensitivity_tbl %>%
  kbl(caption = "Sensitivity check: key inferential p-values with vs without RT 3-SD filtering",
      col.names = c("Analysis", "p (unfiltered)", "p (filtered)",
                    "Sig unfiltered (alpha=.05)", "Sig filtered (alpha=.05)",
                    "Decision stable?")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

**Observation (sensitivity check):**
`r sum(sensitivity_tbl$Decision_stable == "Yes")` out of `r nrow(sensitivity_tbl)`
inferential decisions are unchanged after applying the RT 3-SD filter. The hypothesis-level
conclusions (RQ1 accuracy supported, RQ2 supported, RQ3 not supported as originally predicted,
interaction non-significant) remain the same.

  ## Hypothesis Evaluation and Conclusion

  ### Hypothesis matching

  1. **RQ1 (overall condition effect): Supported.**
    NB participants are significantly more accurate than AB participants. RT does not
    show a reliable condition difference.
  2. **RQ2 (BB: NB > AB): Supported.**
    BB accuracy is significantly higher in NB than AB.
  3. **RQ3 (EM: NB ~ AB / no difference): Not supported as originally predicted.**
    EM also shows a significant NB > AB difference. However, the GLMM interaction is
    non-significant, indicating the condition advantage is broadly similar across BB and EM.

  ### Overall conclusion

  Across trial-level and subject-level analyses, natural-transition viewing yields higher
  recognition accuracy than abrupt-cut viewing. The disadvantage for abrupt cuts is not
  restricted only to BB items; rather, it appears as a general condition-level decrement in
  recognition. At the same time, EM items are remembered better than BB items within both
  conditions, suggesting a stable event-middle advantage in this dataset.

# Phase 2 Summary

| Step | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Recruitment & exclusions | 184 recruited → **166 retained** (1 corrupt file + 4 vigilance failures) |
| Data cleaning | Removed encoding-phase rows + applied RT 3-SD outlier rule for inferential analyses |
| Demographics | Included and reported all available demographic fields (Age, Gender, Handedness, Vision, plus any additional columns) |
| Descriptive accuracy | AB = **83.8%**, NB = **87.0%** |
| Condition × target type | NB > AB for both BB and EM; condition × target-type interaction not significant in GLMM |
| REC | NB shows higher bias-corrected discrimination than AB |
| Normality (Shapiro-Wilk) | AB: W = 0.957, *p* = .009; NB: W = 0.942, *p* = .0007 — **both non-normal** |
| Inferential framework | Non-parametric pairwise tests + **binomial GLMM** for condition × target-type interaction |

| TA item | Implemented in this report |
|---|---|
| Record that clips were already annotated | Yes (Methods → Stimuli and Design) |
| Confidence line + scatter chart | Yes (Extended Visualisations → confidence calibration) |
| Remove RT outliers using 3-SD rule | Yes (Data Cleaning + RT plots/models use cleaned RT) |
| Check EM > BB within each group | Yes (paired Wilcoxon in inferential section) |
| Replace mixed ANOVA with GLMM | Yes (binomial GLMM with subject/item random intercepts) |
| Include all demographic fields | Yes (full completeness + pooled + condition-wise tables) |

Global significance threshold: **α = .05**.
